questions.stem: An article costing ₹500 is sold at ₹600. The profit percent is:
questions.explanation: Profit = 100 on CP 500 → 20 %. Direct one-step recognition item, representative of Bank Clerk / SSC CHSL tier.

questions.stem: An article sold at ₹810 at a 10 % LOSS had a cost price of:
questions.explanation: SP = 90 % of CP → 810 = 0.9 CP → CP = 900. Direct inverse.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks his goods 25 % above cost price and offers 10 % discount. His profit percent is:
questions.explanation: Successive +25 %, −10 %: net = 25 − 10 − (25×10)/100 = 15 − 2.5 = +12.5 %. Verify: CP 100 → MP 125 → SP 112.5. Two-step skill, typical CGL Tier-1 / PO-Prelims.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: By selling 11 apples for ₹10, a vendor loses 10 %. To gain 10 %, he should sell how many apples for ₹10?
questions.explanation: At 11 for ₹10 and 10 % loss, CP of 1 apple = (10/11) × (1/0.9) ≈ 1.0101. For 10 % gain, new SP per apple = 1.0101 × 1.10 ≈ 1.1111 = 10/9. So 9 apples for ₹10. Classic 'quantity per rupee' inversion.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.topic: Profit & Loss — Clerk → CGL → PO-Mains tier spread

questions.stem: A trader sells two articles at the same price. On one he earns 20 % profit and on the other a 20 % loss. His net profit/loss percent is:
questions.explanation: 'Same SP, equal & opposite %' → ALWAYS a NET LOSS = x²/100 % = 400/100 = 4 %. Verify: CP-gain = SP/1.2, CP-loss = SP/0.8; total CP = SP·(1/1.2 + 1/0.8) = SP·(5/6 + 5/4) = SP·(25/12). Total SP = 2·SP. Loss/total CP = (SP·1/12)/(SP·25/12) = 1/25 = 4 %.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks up his goods by 50 %. He offers successive discounts of 10 % and 20 %. The single-equivalent discount if he marketed directly at his desired final price would be:
questions.explanation: Two successive discounts of a % and b %: equivalent = a + b − (ab)/100 = 10 + 20 − 2 = 28 %. (Mark-up is a red herring for THIS sub-question; the equivalent-discount rule acts only on the two discounts.)

questions.stem: A dishonest dealer professes to sell at cost price, but uses a 960 g weight for 1 kg AND marks his goods 10 % above cost. His overall gain is closest to:
questions.explanation: Layered gain. Let CP of 1000 g = 100 → CP of 960 g (actually delivered) = 96. Marked price for '1 kg' = 110. Customer pays 110 but receives 960 g whose true CP is 96. Profit = 14 on CP 96 → 14.58 %. Good UPSC-prelims / Mains-level multi-factor problem.

questions.stem: The ratio of cost price to selling price of an article is 4 : 5. The profit percent is:
questions.explanation: Take CP = 4, SP = 5. Profit = 1 on CP 4 → 25 %. Fast ratio-to-percent conversion, standard CGL Tier-1 item.
